name: GameDay

persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Mike, 62. Your granddaughter Emma, 12, plays basketball for a team called Gold Rush in your church's Saturday league. Today is Friday night, you are driving her tomorrow, and you need to know where and when she plays, and what to bring.

challenge.intro: Now you are Mike, and Emma plays for Gold Rush. Nobody will tell you where to look. Find each answer on the page and write it in the box under the job. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Use the NORMAL app link (not the 🧪 test copy). Open GameDay. If the welcome card shows, tap 'skip the tour' → 'Let’s go ›'. There is nothing to erase: GameDay never saves anything you type.
challenge.challengeNote: GameDay saves nothing on the phone. Families only read the page; the league director writes the schedule into the app itself. So the app cannot be 'started empty' and no answer can be read from localStorage. Every task is a find-it question the student answers in writing (check = null, selfReport). The dates follow today (the example league always shows next Saturday), so the answers stay the same all week.

tasks.text: When is Gold Rush's next game, at what time, and against which team?
tasks.selfReport: Write the day, the time and the other team.
tasks.answer: This coming Saturday at 9:00 AM, against Blue Thunder (first card under Upcoming games).
tasks.hint: Look under Upcoming games. The first card is the next game day. Find the line with Gold Rush.

tasks.text: Emma has practice every week. Which day and what time?
tasks.selfReport: Write the day and the time.
tasks.hint: Scroll down past the table to Practice times.

tasks.text: Which team is first in the league right now, and how many games has it won and lost?
tasks.selfReport: Write the team and its wins and losses.
tasks.answer: Blue Thunder, 2 wins and 0 losses (the crown in Standings).
tasks.hint: Look at the Standings table. W means wins, L means losses.

tasks.text: You arrive at the gym. Which door do you use, and what must Emma bring with her?
tasks.selfReport: Write the door and what to bring.
tasks.answer: Door 4, by the playground; bring her own water bottle (The gym, at the bottom).
tasks.hint: The very last card on the page, The gym, tells you.

tasks.text: On Saturday morning there is heavy snow. How will you know quickly if the games are cancelled?
tasks.selfReport: Write where you would look and what you would see.
tasks.answer: A red banner appears at the very top of the page (the league director puts it there). No phone calls needed.
tasks.hint: Think about the video: what appears at the top of the page when games are cancelled?

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: one page for a church sports league: games, standings, practice times, the gym
families only read it; the league leader updates it for everyone
a red banner at the top tells everyone at once when games are cancelled

personaChurch.title: Pretend you are…
personaChurch.text: Pretend you are Mike, 34, the youth pastor who runs your church's Saturday basketball league. Parents keep calling with the same questions. Tonight Emma's grandfather calls: when and where does her team, Gold Rush, play, and what should she bring? You check that the league page answers it all.

introChurch: Now you are Mike, the youth pastor. Nobody will tell you where to look. Find each answer on the page and write it in the box under the job. When you finish, tap Check my work.

lines: This is GameDay. In the next few minutes you will see what it is for, who it is for, and how to read it.
Here is the everyday problem. A church runs a basketball league for kids. Six teams, and maybe forty families.
Every week the families ask the same questions. When is our game? Who do we play? When is practice? Which door of the gym do we use?
And on a snow day, the league director phones forty families, one by one. Someone always hears too late and drives to an empty gym.
GameDay puts all of it on one page. Every family keeps the same link. The league director writes the schedule once, and everyone reads it.
It is for parents, players, and grandparents, who read it, and for the league director, who keeps it up to date.
Families only read. There is nothing to sign up for, nothing to type, and nothing to save.
There are no tabs. It is one page, top to bottom. At the top is the name, GameDay, and the name of the league.
This one is an example league with made-up teams, and a box with a dashed border says so. Your league director puts the real schedule in.
Just under the top is the spot for the red banner. Most days it is empty, so you do not see it.
When games are cancelled, the league director puts a line there, like this example. It is the first thing every family sees. That one banner replaces forty phone calls.
Next comes Upcoming games, grouped by day. Each day has its own card with the date at the top.
On each line you see the two teams, the gym, and on the right, the time of the game.
Games already played drop off by themselves. So the first card is always the next game day.
Then Standings. W means wins and L means losses. The team on top wears a crown. Teams with the same record show a T before their place, for tied.
Then Practice times. Each team has its evening of the week, with start and end times.
At the bottom is The gym: its name and address, which door to use, when the snack stand is open, and what to bring.
Your first two minutes: open the link, find your team's next game, and check its practice night.
Then add it to your Home Screen from the Share button, so it is one tap away on game day.
Make it a habit: open GameDay before you drive. No red banner means you are playing.
For the league director: you fill in the teams, games, practices, and gym once, in one short block of the app's file. After each game day, you update the wins and losses.
Nothing is collected from families. There are no accounts, no group texts, and no ads to your parents. The schedule still reads without a connection.
GameDay comes with the Church membership, for every season of your league.
And the round question mark button has text size, the tour, and help, any time. Profits help students in Kenya stay in school.

explore.try: Read the address and details. Turn the phone sideways and back.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
